races.name: Racing TV Club Day EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Welcome Racing TV Club Members Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Concert Pitch
runners_data.note: Consistent runner with six career starts, all placed in similar good ground conditions over 5f; sits naturally prominent, ideally suited to tracking Mrs Mole and striking late, and Brian Ellison's yard has shown recent form with 2 wins from 16 runners in 14 days — no concerns.

runners_data.name: Enemy Action
runners_data.note: Has placed at 5f on good ground and wears a hood, which should aid concentration; natural hold-up style means he will be further back than ideal, though a genuinely stronger pace would bring him into play — trainer Ollie Pears has had a quiet 14-day spell with 0 from 5.

runners_data.name: Mrs Mole
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who should control the tempo entirely on her own terms; has handled good ground across all three starts and drops back to 5f from 6-7f which suits a pace-setter — Steph Hollinshead runners have been light on winners recently but this is her optimal tactical scenario.

runners_data.name: Mardy Bum
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's hold-up type has placed three times over 5-6f on good ground and races with a hood; naturally suited to coming from the rear but will be closer to midfield in this compressed shape, which may actually help him sustain his effort better than the true closers behind him.

runners_data.name: Lairy Mary
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly has a course-and-distance win over this track and going, and her prominent style is a natural fit for the shape this race will take; Duran Fentiman rode her to that win and that combination is worth noting — she arrives on just 20 days' rest and looks tactically well positioned.

runners_data.name: Kaiulani Spirit
runners_data.note: Three-run two-year-old without a win or place on genuinely good ground, and her best form came over 5f on softer conditions; wears a hood and races for Tim Easterby but the sim-going record of 0W0P over comparable surfaces raises a query about her ability to fire here — natural hold-up style adds further positional concern.

runners_data.name: Johns Power
runners_data.note: Roger Fell runner whose true racing style is at the back of the field, though the race shape forces him into a midfield map position that is not natural to him; form reads 0-6-4 with no win or place in comparable conditions and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 reflects the genuine disadvantage of racing out of role.

runners_data.name: Targa
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's 5-run two-year-old has placed once over 5f on good ground but has been fading in the assessments; instinctively a hold-up horse whose chance is compressed by the field structure — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 tempers expectations, and his overall record over 5f on good ground shows no wins.

runners_data.name: Good Fighter
runners_data.note: Runs in blinkers for Ismail Mohammed & Jose Santos and is a genuine hold-up type now slotted into midfield by necessity, not by nature; three career runs have produced 9th, 5th and 7th — the blinkers may sharpen his early response but his style and form profile make him a long shot in this shape.

runners_data.name: Articulate
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost's two-year-old has a flag for fading in finishes, which is a serious concern in a race where she will not get the strong late pace that might otherwise compress the field for a closer; all three career starts have been over 5f on good ground with a best of 5th, and racing out of her natural rearward position only adds to the difficulty.

races.paceDynamic: Mrs Mole is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to match her stride for stride from the gates, she should secure an uncontested lead at a sustainable clip on this good-to-firm 5f Beverley straight. Concert Pitch and Lairy Mary will press forward from their prominent positions and sit just off the pace, giving the race a workable tempo rather than a frantic one — enough to keep Mrs Mole honest but not enough to burn her off. The field carries a significant volume of hold-up intent: Johns Power, Targa, Good Fighter and Articulate are all natural rear-of-field operators redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the race shape has no room for them at the back, meaning their true style is largely negated here. That compression of hold-up horses into the middle of the pack favours early-to-race, prominent types who can travel into a steady gallop and sustain their effort — front-running and prominent profiles are the clear tactical beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Mrs Mole breaks cleanly and settles into her natural front-running rhythm with no rival willing to match her early.
scenarios.body: Mrs Mole dictates a measured but honest pace, conserving enough energy to repel challengers in the final furlong on the good-to-firm ground she has handled before; Concert Pitch and Lairy Mary sit ideally poised just off the pace and are best-placed to pounce if she ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Concert Pitch or Lairy Mary travel strongly just off Mrs Mole and have enough in reserve to reel her in close home.
scenarios.body: The early pace is controlled enough that neither prominent runner burns excessive energy, and the good-to-firm 5f suits a horse who can quicken off that tempo; Lairy Mary's course-and-distance win over this track and going gives her the profile edge here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than anticipated and front horses tie up inside the final furlong, allowing a midfield finisher to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Mardy Bum has placed consistently over 5-6f on good ground and, racing off a genuine pace, could sustain a run from midfield better than the redistibuted true hold-up types; Enemy Action has placed in similar conditions and could also benefit if there is any late attrition through the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early, setting up an unusually strong late sectional that allows one of the genuine rear-of-field operators to finish past exhausted rivals.
scenarios.body: Johns Power, Targa or Good Fighter would need their natural position and a collapse of the front end to be competitive — a scenario made unlikely by the sustainable tempo Mrs Mole typically sets and by the fact all three are racing out of role in this shape; the low probability reflects the structural disadvantage all three face here.

watchPoints.text: Mrs Mole's gate — if Clifford Lee gets her away cleanly and unopposed she could control the pace entirely; any slow break changes the shape of the whole race immediately.

Lairy Mary and Concert Pitch tracking each other — both prominent types could cancel each other out if they race too keenly trying to close on Mrs Mole in the first two furlongs, compromising their respective finishing kicks.

The four redistributed hold-up horses (Johns Power, Targa, Good Fighter, Articulate) will all be bunched in midfield rather than at the rear — watch for traffic issues and interference in the straight as they look for gaps in a compressed middle section.

Mardy Bum's hood and consistent placing record over 5f on good ground makes him the most credible threat from off the pace if the front end does come back; watch how Mark Winn positions him in the early strides relative to the midfield cluster.

races.name: Hornsea Ladies At The Races Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Claret And Blues
runners_data.note: Modest form string of 53665 with no wins or places on similar going; a natural closer whose true running style sits at the rear of the field — the midfield map position overstates how comfortably she can travel in that role here, and the style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Court Legend
runners_data.note: Tagged with a fades-in-finish warning and a 34-day absence on a 0W0P record over 6f Good — stepping up to 7½f for the first time is a significant ask, and Billy Garritty's sole task will be managing the stamina question.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Beach
runners_data.note: Recent 3rd over 6f Good (form: 5603) represents the best recent result among the redistributed hold-up horses; Sam James is a strong booking from Ollie Sangster's yard, but this horse's natural race position is further back than the map suggests — the style-fit discount tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Bonjour Belle
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's filly is on a 6-day turnaround alongside stablemate Amantha, showing the yard is primed; her four runs have all come over 7f and she has placed once at 4th on Good, but she is a true hold-up type pushed into a midfield slot that doesn't suit her natural pattern.

runners_data.name: Ariane Sky
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field — won last time over 8f Good at Goodwood, confirming the trip is within range; Mason Paetel takes a 5lb claim for James Owen's in-form operation (7 wins from 48 in 14 days) and faces no pace rival to challenge her lead.

runners_data.name: State Of Gold
runners_data.note: Runner-up over 6f Good last time gives him a solid form line; William Pyle rides for the low-strike-rate Craig Lidster yard (0/8 in 14 days), and a 56-day break adds a freshness question — his natural hold-up style means he will need things to happen in front of him.

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: The most consistent horse in the race with a 1W4P record across seven runs on Good ground, including three consecutive placed efforts over 7f; Brian Ellison has her fit off a 6-day turnaround and Ben Robinson retains the ride — her profile of tracking prominently and sustaining a challenge suits the expected race shape best.

runners_data.name: Farndale
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly has four runs over 7-8f without winning or placing on Good ground; a 40-day layoff and a style-fit score of 0.92 suggest she will be shuffled further back than she wants when the gates open, weakening her chance.

runners_data.name: Wells Fargo Stage
runners_data.note: Three runs, 0W0P, fades-in-finish tag, and a 38-day absence all point the wrong way; Duran Fentiman inherits a horse that found only 9th over 6f Good last time and whose redistribution to midfield masks an even deeper natural position.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire Dream
runners_data.note: Lowest OR in the field at 48 with three runs yielding only a 5th on Good ground as best effort; Andrew Mullen will face a stiff task coaxing Yorkshire Dream into any challenging position from 47 days off, and the style-fit discount on her midfield slot compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Whisper Angel
runners_data.note: Fades-in-finish tag and a 13-day turnaround for Nigel Tinkler, who has 4 wins from 29 in the last fortnight; three runs over 6-7f Good/Standard without threatening a place, and the 3lb claim from Alex Jary only partially offsets the weight of evidence against her.

races.paceDynamic: Ariane Sky is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner nursery and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to challenge her for the lead — she will bowl along from the gates at whatever tempo suits Mason Paetel and James Owen's team, who won on her last time at Goodwood over 8f on Good ground. Behind her, the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types: Claret And Blues, Sovereign Beach, Bonjour Belle, Farndale, Wells Fargo Stage, Yorkshire Dream, and Whisper Angel are all natural hold-up horses whose map positions have been redistributed forward to midfield simply because there is no room for all of them at the rear — Amantha and State Of Gold are the most credible of those with genuine placed form to press closer to the pace. On Good to Firm ground over 7½f at Beverley, a lone leader dictating a sustainable gallop will get a significant sectional advantage and the race shape heavily favours anything that can sit close to the pace and travel — Amantha, with her seven-furlong placed form on Good ground (3-3-2-1), is the horse best positioned to exploit this front-runner-friendly shape by tracking Ariane Sky from a prominent berth. The field contains more hold-up types than can naturally find their position, with Ariane Sky almost certain to secure the rail lead, and Amantha and State Of Gold the most likely to land the closest tracking roles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ariane Sky Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ariane Sky bowls along uncontested and sets a sustainable Good-to-Firm gallop that stretches the field entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Ariane Sky gets a soft lead, controls the fractions, and the hold-up horses stranded in midfield never generate the momentum to reel her in; her Goodwood 8f win on Good shows she stays and quickens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to tire Ariane Sky but Amantha or State Of Gold have tracked closely enough to collar her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Amantha's sequence of 3-3-2-1 over 7f on Good ground makes her the standout tracker, with the fitness edge of a 6-day turnaround from Brian Ellison's yard suiting a horse that has clearly been kept fresh for this; State Of Gold's runner-up over 6f on Good also gives him the profile to challenge if held up just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ariane Sky goes too fast early on Good to Firm and opens a gap for a closer to come from off the pace in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: This is structurally the least likely shape given the lone, sustainable pace, but Sovereign Beach's recent 3rd over 6f on Good shows enough ability to benefit if the field fans wide and the pace collapses; Claret And Blues has the highest style-fit score among redistributed runners and could land this if the pace turns frantic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If Ariane Sky is content to jog along and the field concertinas, triggering a sprint finish that negates any positional advantage.
scenarios.body: A bunched, sprint-finish scenario suits the horse with the most raw speed in the final furlong, but with most runners showing 0W0P on similar going and fading-in-finish tags on Court Legend, Wells Fargo Stage, and Whisper Angel, the beneficiaries would be limited; Amantha's placed consistency still gives her the edge even in a flat-out sprint.

watchPoints.text: Amantha (Ellison/Robinson) arrives fit off a 6-day turnaround with a 1W4P record over 7f on Good — watch her position out of the gates; if she slots second or third behind Ariane Sky she becomes the primary danger to the front-runner.

Ariane Sky is alone in front and Mason Paetel's use of a 5lb claim means she carries a competitive weight — watch whether she is allowed to stride on or is restrained, as the tempo she sets will define every other scenario in this race.

State Of Gold's 56-day absence and the Lidster yard's 0/8 strike rate in the last 14 days are a combination worth monitoring in the betting ring — a market move from a long price would suggest connections believe the layoff has not blunted his form.

Bonjour Belle and Amantha are both trained by Brian Ellison and arrive on identical 6-day turnarounds — watch which of the two the yard's market support follows, as that will indicate which runner Ellison considers live.

Wells Fargo Stage, Court Legend, and Whisper Angel all carry fades-in-finish warnings — if the pace is strong and the field strings out, these three are the most likely to drop away in the final 2f and their early positions should not be misread as a sign of competitive engagement.

races.name: Connexin Super Fast Sprint Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Call To Action
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with genuine claims — two 2nd-place finishes from his last five starts at 5f on good, and trainer Easterby has three winners from 23 in the last 14 days; 70 days off is the only query, but his going record (8 from 11 in similar conditions) is strong.

runners_data.name: Holbache
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 8-year-old who has won at 6f on good for Julie Camacho and is most effective when tracking a single front-runner — dropping to 5f is the slight query, having done all his best work at 6f in his recent history.

runners_data.name: Castan
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has run 11 and 9 in his two most recent 5f-good runs — the form string reads poorly and Bryan Smart's T14 of 1 from 7 is modest; only 12 days since last run suggests he's in a busy campaign without finding form.

runners_data.name: American Bay
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's prominent racer has consistent Beverley-style flat 5f form (12 of 15 from similar going) and finished 2nd recently at this trip — Jason Hart is an able partner for a stalking role just off Ingleby Archie, making this profile very well suited to the race shape.

runners_data.name: Good Earth
runners_data.note: 9-year-old hold-up horse who posted a 2nd at 5f on good earlier in the season and finished 4th and 5th in similar company recently; Tom Eaves provides strong northern experience but the age and recent 5th-18th run sequence suggests he needs a perfect pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Ingleby Archie
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, whose record of 2 wins and 7 places from 12 starts on similar going underlines his consistency; 20 days since last run is fine, and dictating a solo lead over this straight 5f on good-to-firm is exactly his comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Ventura Express
runners_data.note: 9-year-old hold-up type who has found the frame at 5f on good (4th, 6th, 4th, 5th recently) but without winning — David Nolan's placing will need the pace to collapse to bring him into play, which is unlikely with only one front-runner setting an honest gallop.

runners_data.name: Squealer
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 6-year-old has a decent 1W4P record from similar going and his three 5f-good runs in recent form show consistency; however, his natural style is genuine hold-up and he is mapped to midfield only because of the congestion at the rear — his effective racing position may not be achievable here, tempering expectations.

runners_data.name: Shazani
runners_data.note: Dropped in from 6-7f to 5f, the 4-year-old has placed recently (2nd and 3rd in his last four) and shows good form on good going; Roy Bowring's horse is a prominent type who could benefit from tracking Ingleby Archie, though the trip shortening is an unknown.

runners_data.name: Infinity Blue
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 5-year-old returns from a 304-day absence — that layoff is the dominant flag, and while he placed well (3rd, 2nd) at 5-6f on good in 2023-24, a horse racing for the first time in 10 months who is also unable to secure his preferred deep hold-up berth faces a very difficult task here.

runners_data.name: Jojo Rabbit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr has 5 winners from 23 in 14 days, keeping this one in view, and Jojo Rabbit has placed twice at 5f on good recently; the key caveat is that his true style is waiting off the pace, yet in a field this congested with hold-up types he is unlikely to get the uncontested rear position he needs to deliver his finish.

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: Brian Rothwell's lowest-rated runner (OR 57) whose trainer has 0 from 2 in the last 14 days; he has won at 5f on good going but his recent 8th-8th-12th sequence at this trip suggests he needs a very specific set of circumstances, and being a genuine hold-up type unable to settle at the back further reduces his prospects.

races.paceDynamic: Ingleby Archie is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival prepared to contest the lead, Jack Garritty can dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front on good-to-firm ground at Beverley's straight 5f. American Bay and Holbache will push forward to prominent positions just behind, creating a settled pace shape rather than a hot-speed duel. The redistribution note is important: Squealer, Jojo Rabbit, Infinity Blue, and Opal Storm are all genuine hold-up types but are shown in midfield because this field contains more deep closers than the map can accommodate at the rear — of those, only Squealer and Jojo Rabbit have the course and distance profiles to partially compensate, but neither is likely to get a true waiting ride. This race shape — a single front-runner setting a sustainable pace with a compressed mid-pack — historically favours horses who race prominently or in the first half of the field and can kick off the bend, with pure hold-up horses at a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Archie Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ingleby Archie bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but not suicidal pace, allowing prominent horses to track and pounce.
scenarios.body: Ingleby Archie's natural front-running style on good-to-firm over 5f at Beverley suits him perfectly, and with American Bay and Holbache stalking, one of that tracking trio will have the legs at the furlong pole; this is the dominant shape here given the single pace-setter and compressed field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Ingleby Archie sets a slightly faster-than-usual gallop and ties up late, allowing the horses mapped to midfield to run through.
scenarios.body: Call To Action and Good Earth, who have genuine hold-up credentials and are correctly positioned behind midfield, could benefit if the front end fades; Call To Action's two recent 2nd-place finishes at 5f on good ground make him the prime beneficiary in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Squealer or Jojo Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the redistribution matters less than expected, allowing the true hold-up horses to find daylight late.
scenarios.body: Squealer has strong good-going course form at 5f and Jojo Rabbit has hit the frame repeatedly at this trip, so if gaps open they carry the best class-adjusted back-end pace of the group; however, both are racing out of their natural position which structurally reduces their chance, hence the discounted probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Dominates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Ingleby Archie goes unchallenged and the pace is so controlled that he simply stays on strongest all the way to the line.
scenarios.body: On good-to-firm, a relaxed front-runner who has won and placed repeatedly at 6f on similar ground (Ingleby Archie: 2W7P from sim-going history) could simply outstay rivals who never get into a rhythm chasing; Holbache, who has won at 6f on good ground, would be best placed of the hold-up-turned-prominent types to follow if Archie weakens slightly.

watchPoints.text: Ingleby Archie and Jack Garritty — if they are allowed to stride out and set an unchallenged tempo, the entire field will struggle to reel them in on good-to-firm ground; watch the first furlong to see whether anyone pushes up to press.

American Bay — Jason Hart is likely to position him prominently right away, and if he can get the rail or a clear sightline behind Ingleby Archie he becomes the primary danger horse for the dominant scenario.

Squealer, Jojo Rabbit, and Opal Storm — all genuine hold-up types who may find themselves shuffled into midfield rather than their preferred deep position; if they cannot drop in and settle, their late runs will lack the usual punch and their odds may flatter them.

Call To Action — 70 days off is worth monitoring in the paddock and at the start; if he loads and breaks cleanly, his good-going 5f record suggests he could outfinish the other hold-up horses even if the pace does not collapse.

Infinity Blue — 304 days since last run is a significant flag; track his paddock behaviour and early gallop, as a horse returning from such a long absence rarely produces its best first time back, particularly in a competitive sprint handicap.

races.name: Middle Distance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Return With Gold
runners_data.note: Sole pace-setter here and will lead unchallenged over 1m4f on Good to Firm, but its recent form reads 131-40 and similar-going figures are modest (0W, 0P from 2 runs); effective style fit at this track but raw form profile is fragile for a horse expected to dictate.

runners_data.name: Sisterandbrother
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with three wins from 15 runs on similar ground — solid but limited; in truth a pure hold-up horse by nature, though the compressed field may drag it closer to the pace than connections would ideally want, reducing its ability to produce a sustained late run.

runners_data.name: Grey Fable
runners_data.note: Trainer Karl Thornton has landed 1 from 2 in the past 14 days suggesting live stable form, and the horse wore a hood (hg:t) last time; its natural style is to come from well off the pace, yet the lone front-runner scenario means the cavalry charge it needs to exploit may simply not materialise on this going.

runners_data.name: Wardlaw
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old arrives 48 days freshened up after two consecutive runner-up finishes at 14f on Good ground — the most relevant form profile in the field for today's conditions; a genuine hold-up operator whose patient placing suits a race where the late challenge will be decisive.

runners_data.name: That Darn Cantor
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride for Ed Dunlop on a three-year-old placed in six consecutive runs on Good ground, making it the most reliable at-the-money performer here; a hold-up type whose consistent form at 12f suggests the extra 2f on Good to Firm is the key unknown, though Dunlop's horses tend to improve with the step up.

runners_data.name: Mr Moonshine
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey yard in decent form (3/30 over 14 days) and Oisin Orr is a positive booking; naturally a hold-up horse at heart, yet the crowded rear means it is mapped to midfield — a position that may actually suit its tendency to travel kindly before producing a late effort on Good ground, where it has placed three times from five starts.

races.paceDynamic: Return With Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, unchallenged gallop over Beverley's 1m4f on Good to Firm ground. The pace is unlikely to be searching — one horse setting its own rhythm on a flat track in a handicap of this modest grade typically produces a moderate tempo that suits those travelling well within themselves. Five of the six runners are hold-up or prominent types by nature, but the map can only absorb so many at the rear, meaning the race shape consolidates into a compact bunch tracking Return With Gold rather than stringing out. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a sustainable but not punishing tempo — favours hold-up horses with a genuine turn of foot and the ability to quicken on Good to Firm turf, particularly those who have placed consistently at this trip and going; Wardlaw, That Darn Cantor and Mr Moonshine are most likely to secure the midfield positions closest to the pace, while Grey Fable, Sisterandbrother and Mr Moonshine (true rear-ground types) may find themselves shuffled back further than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Late Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Return With Gold sets a steady, uncontested tempo and the field travels in a tight pack, allowing the strongest stayer to pounce in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Return With Gold's solo lead produces a falsely steady gallop that compresses the field, turning the race into a sprint for home from the two-furlong pole; horses with the best turn of foot on Good to Firm ground will dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace proves even more moderate than expected and Return With Gold, unexposed at this trip, steals first run turning for home and is never caught.
scenarios.body: A relaxed journey in front on Good to Firm ground allows Return With Gold to conserve energy and quicken away from a field that leaves the challenge too late; the proximity of the closely-bunched pack may actually work against those who need clear daylight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Early
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse breaks cover earlier than expected at the three-furlong mark and catches the field flat-footed before the home straight develops.
scenarios.body: A runner travelling smoothly in mid-division decides to challenge before the final bend, gaining a significant lead over rivals who are still balanced and waiting; this shape suits those with course experience at longer trips on fast ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rear-Ground Types Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If a stronger-than-anticipated pace develops through the middle stages, stringing out the field and leaving the true hold-up horses with ground to make up but a genuine target to aim at.
scenarios.body: Grey Fable, Sisterandbrother and Mr Moonshine are all natural hold-up operators who would relish a true-run race, but the redistribution caveat means this shape depends on a scenario that requires an untypically demanding tempo that the single front-runner is unlikely to generate.

watchPoints.text: Return With Gold sets a potentially falsely slow tempo unchallenged — watch for any acceleration in the final 3f that catches the chasing pack wrong-footed and delivers a shock hold-on win at a price.

Wardlaw is 48 days off the track for Sir Mark Prescott, a trainer renowned for placing horses to maximum effect when fresh — any market support at the off should be treated as a significant signal given its identical 14f Good-ground profile.

That Darn Cantor has been placed on all six runs on Good ground but has not yet won — watch whether Cieren Fallon attempts an earlier challenge than expected at the 3f pole to break its duck rather than replicating the hold-up tactics that keep producing near-misses.

Grey Fable, Sisterandbrother and Mr Moonshine are all true rear-ground operators crammed into an identical race position — monitor how quickly they settle and whether any one of them is pushed forward early by its jockey to secure a better berth than the map suggests.

The going for this race is officially Good to Firm, slightly faster than the headline 'Good' declaration — any horse whose historical form cluster sits on soft or standard (Sisterandbrother: 3W from 15 on similar) may underperform relative to market expectation on the quicker surface.

races.name: Racing Again On Saturday 29 August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Back From Dubai
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who sets the pace here; trainer Roy Bowring has a 1/3 record over 14 days but Back From Dubai's recent similar-going figures (0 wins, 0 places from 5) temper confidence despite the clear positional advantage of being uncontested in front.

runners_data.name: Copper And Five
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's ten-year-old has a solid recent record at eight furlongs on Good ground (1W, 2P from 10 runs), carries headgear, and is best placed tactically as the only horse likely to track the leader throughout — form figures of 2-2-4 in the last five comparable runs are compelling.

runners_data.name: Ten Sixty Six
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse with three placed efforts from nine runs on Good ground; 33 days since last run is not a concern, but the style demands a strong gallop to peg back, which looks scarce here.

runners_data.name: Dumfries
runners_data.note: James Sullivan rides this consistent Ruth Carr six-year-old who has five consecutive placed or close finishes but no win in those runs; holds his position well mid-to-rear and needs a truly run race to express his stamina at this trip.

runners_data.name: Amarachi
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride on this Joseph Parr four-year-old returning from a 167-day absence; similar-going figures from Southwell are entirely different to Beverley on Good to Firm, and the long layoff makes fitness an open question despite placed efforts last season.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Daragh Bourke's three-year-old won at eight furlongs on Good ground most recently and is a true hold-up horse by inclination, though the compressed field means it is likely to race further forward than ideal — its STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects the positional compromise, and five days since last run is a minor flag.

runners_data.name: Sweet Cicely
runners_data.note: Mike Sowersby's four-year-old has raced consistently over twelve to sixteen furlongs and drops in trip here; a genuine hold-up racer by style, it is placed in midfield on the map only because the rear is congested — its stamina profile may suit if the race gets run at a genuine pace, though recent form figures show no wins or places.

runners_data.name: Aurora's Doublesix
runners_data.note: Faye McManoman rides this Brian Rothwell four-year-old who carries a noted finishing fade flag and has raced almost exclusively over five to six furlongs — the step up to a mile and a half looks a substantial ask, and its redistribution into midfield rather than the rear does it no stylistic favours.

runners_data.name: Royal Sizzler
runners_data.note: Sean Kirrane partners Michael Dods' three-year-old, a hold-up horse with only four runs to assess and just one placed effort on similar going; 51 days since last run adds a fitness caveat, and the horse is placed in midfield purely because the rear of the map is oversubscribed — its natural instinct is to come from last.

runners_data.name: Harswell River
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's three-year-old has consistent form at ten furlongs on Good ground (0W, 4P from five comparable runs) and apprentice Cian Horgan claims five pounds; despite being a hold-up type by preference, its recent form suggests it tracks reasonably close to the pace and could be the most effective of the redistributed runners if it secures a forward pitch.

races.paceDynamic: Back From Dubai is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, faces no significant pressure for the lead — at a mile and a half on Good to Firm ground at Beverley, that means a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset rather than a searching test. With the pace card showing just one genuine leader and the rest of the field comprised almost entirely of hold-up and midfield types, the race will be run at Back From Dubai's tempo, with Copper And Five likely to track closely from a prominent pitch. The hold-up contingent — Saxon Grace, Royal Sizzler, Harswell River, Sweet Cicely and Aurora's Doublesix — is so large relative to the field that several cannot occupy their natural rear positions and are redistributed into midfield on the map; of those, Harswell River and Saxon Grace are most likely to actually achieve a forward berth given their recent positional patterns. A single unhurried front-runner dictating on a track that rewards those who travel well into the straight points clearly toward horses racing prominently or in the first half of the field getting the clearest run to the line — true deep closers are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Back From Dubai bowls along unchallenged and sets a measured pace that turns the race into a test of staying power from the front.
scenarios.body: Back From Dubai dictates every yard on a track where a lone leader can fill lungs and quicken entering the straight, denying hold-up horses a pace to aim at. Copper And Five, travelling prominently throughout, is best positioned to capitalise if the leader tires, while Ten Sixty Six's hold-up style leaves it needing the leader to come back to the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Copper And Five applies enough sustained pressure through the middle miles to force a genuine contest from the front.
scenarios.body: A competitive duel between the two forward-going runners lifts the pace just enough to bring the race to those tracking in the first half of the field, but not enough to release true back-markers. Harswell River, genuine form at ten furlongs and consistent on Good ground, is the most likely beneficiary from a chasing position if it gets its natural prominent pitch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and horses from the rear of the field produce a late surge.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Back From Dubai to tie up dramatically and the redistributed hold-up types — Saxon Grace, Royal Sizzler — to find room from further back than is natural for them, which is a structural ask given how the field is built. Ten Sixty Six has the best recent placed form at eight furlongs on Good ground and would be the most credible finisher if this shape materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Contested Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is inconsistent — surging and stopping — producing a bunched finish with no clear positional advantage.
scenarios.body: An unpredictable gallop scrambles tactical plans and can throw up any winner, though horses with fitness concerns, long absences like Amarachi (167 days off) or stamina doubts over this trip are most vulnerable. Sweet Cicely's recent form at longer trips gives her a marginal staying edge in a muddled scenario, but overall the field's lack of proven high-class form makes this chaotic outcome unlikely to reward any one profile consistently.

watchPoints.text: Back From Dubai sets a pace entirely of its own choosing — if it finds a low-pressure rhythm and quickens entering Beverley's straight, no hold-up horse may have enough room or momentum to close.

Harswell River and Saxon Grace are both natural hold-up horses who may attempt to race more prominently than usual given the field composition — watch the early positions, as crowding in the first quarter-mile could cause trouble for both.

Amarachi returns from 167 days off and all its form is on Southwell's all-weather; the fitness unknown in a field where small margins matter at this level is a significant risk factor regardless of the race shape.

Aurora's Doublesix has a noted tendency to fade in the finish and has raced almost exclusively at sprint distances — if it is prominent early it may compromise the finish for horses immediately behind it.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race despite the card stating Good — the faster surface suits a controlled front-runner's rhythm and may catch out horses whose best form is on softer ground, particularly Dumfries (three of five runs on Soft or Standard).
